notes:
CRM notes (shorthand, call extracts, POC details)
- Company background: mid-market collaboration SaaS for product teams (doc & meeting summarization, in-app assistant). 250 employees, heavy front-end + server side. 40% of revenue on annual plans.
- Why Redwood: started w/ Hosted API to ship quickly. POC showed 1) good quality on summarization, 2) p95 latency concerns at scale. Now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and to hit SLAs.
- Technical requirements (from SE call 2024-10-23):
  - Workloads: chat sessions (multi-turn), summarization (long docs, up to 8k tokens), embeddings for semantic search + reranking.
  - Latency targets: "must not exceed 150ms p95 for short chat tokens"; end-to-end p95 for summarization acceptable up to 700ms for batched runs.
  - Throughput baseline: 20 concurrent chat streams sustained; peak burst up to 50 concurrent for new feature launch.
  - Model preferences: open Llama-variant for cost; willing to evaluate fine-tuned 7B/13B. Want ability to fall back to cheaper quantized variant.
  - KV cache/long-context support mandatory.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required; enterprise SAML SSO; customer-managed KMS desirable; audit logging + 1 year retention; EU data residency for subset of customers.
- POC acceptance criteria (agreed):
  1) Hosted API POC: Embedding recall >= 0.78 on internal eval set; chat quality bench score >= baseline. (met)
  2) Dedicated perf POC: sustain 20 concurrent chat sessions at p95 <= 150ms for 95% of runs for 1 hour. (running)
  3) Ops checklist: IAM + SSO integration + encrypted logs verified.
- Pricing/packaging negotiation notes (key):
  - QuantumFold is price sensitive; total ARR target ~ $75k-250k. They prefer commit-based pricing with fixed monthly GPU-months + predictable unit token pricing.
  - Requested commitment tiers: 2x, 5x, 10x baseline throughput options. Want clear burst headroom at 1.5-2.0x baseline without renegotiation for short windows.
  - Overage ask: capped % over commit or blended overage price; asked for a 30-day sprint buffer before heavier overage rates kick in.
  - Ramp schedule: 3-month ramp to 60% of committed capacity, 6-month plan to full commit. Want credits for under-use in first 2 months.
  - Payment/term: quarterly invoicing preferred; open to annual if discount >= 20%.
- Competitive notes: they ran small tests against OpenAI and InferDeploy; Redwood stood out for cost per token on long-context + observable traces. Procurement asked for explicit latency SLOs vs competitors.
- Legal/security: procurement pushed back on Redwood CSA indemnity clause; legal drafting changes requested. Also DPA data residency appendix required for EU customers.
- Direct quotes / on-record lines:
  - "We like the throughput but need a clean overage model — can't have surprise bills during product launches." — Head of Engineering
  - "If we can get a 6 month ramp and burst to 2x for launches, we can commit to 10 GPU-months initially." — Procurement
- Next steps / owner actions:
  - AE (Maya) to circulate revised pricing deck w/ 3 commit options + explicit burst SLA by 2024-11-22 (drive link above).
  - SE (Liam) to run dedicated perf POC with 2x burst scenario and share trace exports + p95 report (due 2024-11-27).
  - Legal to exchange redlines on CSA/DPA; Redwood legal + QF legal sync scheduled 2024-11-25.
- Blockers: legal redlines, final budget approval for Q1 ramp, need clearer overage cap math.
- Helpful artifacts: hosted POC logs (internal), eval prompt set (drive), pricing v1 (drive).
